The Africa Credit Rating Agency (AfCRA) — the creation of which African leaders endorsed in 2018 — was ​launched at a ceremony ‌attended by African officials in Port Louis, the capital of Mauritius, where it will be based.

data.title: Eritrean troops reportedly enter Ethiopia’s Tigray region
data.description: Eritrean troops have deployed in Ethiopia's northern Tigray region, multiple sources said Wednesday, threatening to turn an internal conflict into a wider regional war. Fighting broke out between the rebel Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and Ethiopian federal forces on September 23, sparking fears of a return to the devastating 2020-2022 civil war. Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of backing the rebels, and the two neighbours severed diplomatic ties last week.

Her splashdown is scheduled for Thursday off the coast of California.

data.title: 'Most Israeli citizens lost confidence' in govt: Leaders 'shift' blame, 'block' commission inquiry
data.description: Oliver Farry welcomes Guy Poran, a former Israeli Air Force officer and member of Mistaclim (Looking the Occupation in the Eye). Poran sees October 7 as a profound rupture in Israeli society following the unprecedented Hamas attack, which targeted civilians across generations. He argues that responsibility for the failures cannot be separated from the policies that preceded the attack, including the Netanyahu government's approach toward Hamas. Without political change, Poran sees little prospect of repairing relations between Israelis and Palestinians or creating the conditions for a lasting peace, which he regards as crucial to Israel's future.

data.title: No longer the same Israel? October 7 and the future of the Jewish State
data.description: For now, it's still Benjamin Netanyahu's Israel. In 2023, in the immediate aftermath of the country's worst day of bloodshed in its history, pundits predicted the quick demise of the right-wing prime minister. But on the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks, Israel's still not reckoned with the security failures on the day, the root causes of the Hamas-led terror attack, the brutal war of vengeance that followed and above all, Netanyahu is still prime minister with a fair shot at re-election. Even if the Likud leader is voted out on October 27, his most serious election rivals don't exactly advocate for a radical break when it comes to the Palestinians.

data.title: This is one of Norway’s most pristine fjords. So why is it being used as a dumping site for mine waste?
data.description: The Norwegian government has given a permit to a mining company to release waste into Førde fjord despite a 17-year battle by campaigners and a supreme court ruling against it Shortly after the Norwegian stock market closed on 17 June 2026, a few dozen local people from the small west coast town of Vevring crowded around a laptop in a school. Surrounded by children’s drawings and windows looking out over Førde fjord, they listened as news arrived from Oslo. Norway’s supreme court had ruled against its government: a permit to release mining waste directly into the fjord two miles upstream was illegal, the court said. The moment marked the end of a 17-year fight, one of Norway’s most protracted environmental battles in living memory. In Oslo, Ingvild Fonn Asmervik, the project leader for Naturvernforbundet (Friends of the Earth Norway), compared the joy she felt to giving birth to her child. For Anne-Line Thingnes Førsund, a third-generation fisher living on the banks of the fjord in Vevring and a volunteer for the charity’s local branch, it was more of a relief. Like a mountain lifting off her shoulders, she said. Continue reading...

data.title: The dreadful decline of hosting at home: ‘I feel shame any time a friend comes over’
data.description: It used to be quite normal to pop next door for a coffee or invite friends over for dinner. But not any more. What’s behind this change – and just how damaging is it? ‘I really loved hosting at home years ago, before I had kids, when my house wasn’t filled with toys and I had lots of time to plan and shop,” says Rehanna, 41, from Birmingham. Now, if she’s catching up with friends, she would rather go out. “I can’t host and cook at the same time, so if I have people over it will usually be a cold buffet I have made earlier. There are so many really nice restaurants where I live that I’d prefer to go out and try something new than make an old favourite at home.” Personally, I’d never say no to a cold buffet – but Rehanna’s story is not unusual. In the US, the number of people who regularly host friends or family fell from 42% in 1975 to 12% in 2026 – a 70% drop over the last 50 years . In the UK, the numbers are not much better: last year, a poll of 2,000 adults found that more than four in 10 British people avoid hosting at home due to the clean-up it requires. And while chef Nigella Lawson is back on TV screens demonstrating her culinary prowess on The Great British Bake Off, it wasn’t long ago that the self-proclaimed domestic goddess revealed even she had “got out of the habit” of hosting formal dinner parties . Continue reading...

data.title: Germany is right to rearm. But Europe has well-founded fears about that | Paul Taylor
data.description: Berlin’s allies are right to be wary of a sudden surge in German military spending that shuns cooperation with them When the German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, visited the White House earlier this year for a high-stakes meeting with Donald Trump, he invited a Washington-based German researcher little known outside expert circles to a private dinner. Liana Fix had caught his eye with a forthright essay in the journal Foreign Affairs warning of the perils of Germany becoming “Europe’s next hegemon”, whose military dominance may come to scare its neighbours and divide Europe once again. That concern might seem far-fetched after three decades since the fall of the Berlin Wall, during which a peace-loving reunited Germany let its armed forces wither and rust, prided itself on being a “civil power” and preached a gospel of military restraint. Paul Taylor is a senior visiting fellow at the European Policy Centre Continue reading...

data.title: A death, a plagiarism scandal and a quest for revenge: the bizarre tale of Otto Z
data.description: After his mother died, Otto became convinced he’d been wronged by the forensic investigators – and that one of them was a fraud. The truth was even stranger On a balmy, quiet evening in June 2020, Otto’s elderly mother, Doria, was fading in her Munich apartment. As she lay with her eyes closed, her pale face, framed by her white hair, was calm. Otto, masked, gloved and draped in a sterile apron, dozed in a chair beside her. Otto, who sometimes goes by the name Rainer, and whose last name is only known as “Z” because of Germany’s strict privacy laws, was a doctor who had cared for his mother for years, ever since she had suffered a stroke and moved in with him. He described the course of that night to me. He woke to the sound of her short breath and tried to sit her upright. Her eyes were shut, and her lips pursed. She stopped breathing. Otto reached for his phone to call for help, but then Doria opened her eyes and stared into his. She smiled, drew one last deep breath, shut her eyes again, and lay still. Continue reading...

data.title: Canadian poet Anne Carson wins Nobel prize in literature 2026 – live
data.description: Decision announced by permanent secretary of the Swedish Academy Is Can Xue becoming the new Haruki Murakami ? The Japanese literary superstar has for so long been a favourite to win a Nobel without actually winning one that people in the literature industry have started to talk of the “Murakami curse”. But Chinese experimental writer Can Xue too is starting to follow that pattern. A bookies’ top favourite in 2018, 2019, 2023, 2024 and 2025, she’s again topping runners and riders lists this year. Could the pre-announcement hype in itself count against her winning? The Swedish Academy is clearly a self-aware kind of oracle, unhappy to see its choices as determined by outside forces. Last year’s laureate László Krasznahorkai may have been Ladbrokes’ favourite (alongside Can Xue), but bookies correctly predicting the winner is a once-in-a-decade occurrence. The last time it happened before that was with Svetlana Alexievich in 2015, Ladbrokes’ clear favourite at 3/1 odds. Yet while the Academy certainly likes being seen as unpredictable, that’s not to say that it actually is. The biggest literary accolade in the world is evidently engaged in a constant process of re-adjusting the perceived imbalances in its list of laureates. Over the last two decades it has done so in terms of gender, with eight women and 12 men, alternating since 2017, and in terms of crude geography, with 10 winners from western Europe and 10 from the rest of the world. After a Norwegian man in 2023, a South Korean woman in 2024 and a Hungarian man in 2025, we might reasonably expect a non-European woman in 2026. Hence strong odds for Can Xue and Anne Carson , and rumours about Australian memoirist and novelist Alexis Wright and Antiguan-American novelist and gardening writer Jamaica Kincaid . But non-European female is still a very broad category, which is why Nobel-watchers have been considering other patterns. The last Nobel literature laureate known foremost for their poetry was Louise Glück in 2020. Before that, it was Swedish poet Tomas Tranströmer in 2011. High time for another writer of verse, which is why one name bandied about at the Frankfurt Book Fair this week was that of South African poet Marlene van Niek erk . But what if the crucial metric is not literary form but accessibility? The last winners with a genuine populist appeal – writers who didn’t need a Nobel – were Bob Dylan and Kazuo Ishiguro , in 2016 and 2017 respectively. “In a way, it would be logical if this year they wanted someone who was a little more well-known and accessible after Krasznahorkai”, wrote Swedish broadsheet Svenska Dagbladet this week. Jens Liljestrand, a critic for Expressen who predicted Han Kang’s win in 2024, has followed that line of thought and come up with an intriguing prediction: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie , the Nigerian author of the phenomenally successful Half of a Yellow Sun. By that logic, of course, the Academy might have spent the last decade playing one big game of double bluff and working towards handing the prize to Haruki Murakami after all. Continue reading...

Jens Liljestrand, a critic for Expressen who predicted Han Kang’s win in 2024, has followed that line of thought and come up with an intriguing prediction: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie , the Nigerian author of the phenomenally successful Half of a Yellow Sun. By that logic, of course, the Academy might have spent the last decade playing one big game of double bluff and working towards handing the prize to Haruki Murakami after all. Continue reading...

data.title: Why Arturo Béjar left Meta – and blew the whistle: ‘I don’t recall Mark ever being empathetic’
data.description: Béjar’s daughter was 14 when she told him Instagram was failing to keep her safe. So when he became part of Meta’s ‘wellbeing team’, he knew he had to speak out – and his testimony cost it billions The Social Reckoning hits cinemas this Friday, but the real world has already been working on a sequel – or rather, a threequel. Directed by Aaron Sorkin, the movie is a follow-up to The Social Network, detailing the further misadventures of Mark Zuckerberg and his social media empire, and in particular Frances Haugen , the employee who in 2021 leaked internal documents that appeared to show Facebook was aware of the harms its products had inflicted. It’s no spoiler to reveal the film climaxes with Haugen’s testimony to the US Senate, on 5 October 2021. That very same day, Arturo Béjar, a consultant on the wellbeing team of Instagram (which is also owned by Facebook), hit send on a long-gestating email to Zuckerberg and other senior Facebook executives on a similar theme. “I wanted to bring to your attention what I believe is a critical gap in how we as a company approach harm, and how the people we serve experience it,” Béjar began, before laying out some shocking statistics from his team’s survey. For example: 24.4% of 13-15-year-olds on Instagram said they had received unwanted advances, and 21.8% said they had been the target of bullying on the platform in the past seven days . Furthermore, 51% of Instagram users said they had had a bad or harmful experience in the past seven days. Only 1% of them reported it, and of those, 2% had the content taken down – so just 0.02%. This was a far greater degree of harm than the company’s existing measurements suggested. Zuckerberg never replied. Continue reading...

data.title: Rachel Roddy’s recipe for cheese and bread balls | A kitchen in Rome
data.description: These highly crunchable cheesy bread balls are a great way to use up odds and ends Sadly, I’m never going to be able to recreate the cheese and bread balls I made a few weeks ago, because, of the four cheeses used, I recognised only two of them: a bit of gorgonzola and a slice of precious Montgomery cheddar, bought from Da Corrado, a stall on Testaccio market. The other two lumps of cheese, both wrapped in white waxed paper and both quite dry, were, I think, a piece of grana padano and the end of the pecorino we brought back from Umbria. But I can’t be sure, because I didn’t really examine them. Even if I had, it would have been hard to guess; the description “heels of cheese” is appropriate here. What I do know, however, is that the combination of those four grated cheeses with two eggs and enough breadcrumbs to turn the mix into a soft, malleable dough made for fantastic deep-fried balls. The inspiration for using up the uncertain contents of the cheese box was pallotte cacio e ova, which translates as “little cheese and egg balls” , a typical and much-loved thing in both Molise and Abruzzo, which were, in fact, one region until 1964. Pallotte are resourceful, and were surely invented as a way of using up scraps of cheese (almost certainly local pecorino) and bread. Whatever combination of cheese you use, though, the important thing is to add enough soft white breadcrumbs – anything from 80g to 120g – to turn the mixture into a soft dough that you can then mould into balls, but not so compactly that the tenderness is lost. Like meatballs, cheese balls benefit from a rest in the fridge, so they can firm up before frying. The rest in the fridge also ensures that they are cold, which is important, because the thermal shock of the cold surface meeting the hot oil helps create a crisp shell. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Someone else will do it for less’: Refugees in Kenya are powering tech for dwindling pay
data.description: Refugee gig workers for tech companies don’t know how much they’ll be paid – if AI hasn’t already taken their jobs In a portable building in Kakuma, a refugee camp near Kenya ’s northern border with South Sudan , Grace used ChatGPT to research translations of Christian hymns in languages she doesn’t speak. She didn’t know the client, the purpose of her work or whether she would be paid, but as a refugee unable to legally work in Kenya, she needed any opportunity she could get. Grace, who requested anonymity due to a nondisclosure agreement, prompted ChatGPT to translate the hymn’s English text into the assigned east Asian language. She then used the translation to search for existing versions and find information about its translator, author and Christian denomination. She fed those details to AOP Connect, a crowdsourced research platform owned by British AI enterprise software company RWS. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Vibrant, design-led and surprisingly green’: why the Dutch city of Eindhoven is perfect for a relaxed arty break
data.description: After electronics giant Philips left, the city reinvented itself as a multicultural hub for creativity and innovation, and the home of Dutch Design Week A baggily clad skateboarder’s wheels clatter across concrete floors, the noise bouncing off exposed pipes and iron girders. Vaulted skylights set in high ceilings illuminate the industrial space and its central kitchen, from which my main course – a silky lemon risotto, spiked with samphire, rhubarb, garlic, baby onions and basil – has just been transported. I’m in the Dutch city of Eindhoven, in North Brabant, famous for its historic connection to Philips, the one-time electronics giant. The restaurant, Radio Royaal, is housed in what was once their engine room, in the Strijp-S neighbourhood. Today, Strijp-S buzzes with concept stores, an indoor food market, MU Hybrid Art House and the Area 51 skatepark. The broader area, Strijp, was where the company was largely headquartered: its zones are named S, T and R. In the late 90s, Philips withdrew from the city where it had started in 1891, and the letters I, J and P were never assigned. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Those memories are ours and no verdict changes that’: Manchester City fans’ views
data.description: While most supporters seem to want to get behind the club, some fear actions of the owners will divide fanbase Nicola Schofield, City fan for more than 40 years: One of my (million) concerns, as someone who feels angry with the owners, is if the owners’ strategy causes a split in the fanbase. I think everyone wants to get behind the club and team, but this is different to the experience of a relegation of the type I experienced in the 90s. We all shared that, and we stood by the club down to League One and as we came back up. This threatens to be messier, with those who may want the owners out (which is its own minefield) to those who will back them all the way. I think ultimately all fans want to ensure our club still exists, but I do worry at divisions this could cause and that might be hard to heal. Ben, season-ticket holder: I don’t think I have fully processed the news yet. I trusted the club completely and believed every word they said in response to the charges, so this has hit hard. I still think the FFP [financial fair play] rules aren’t fair and never have been. I know that won’t get much sympathy from other fans, and I understand why. Most of them have been waiting for this day for years. Whatever happens, nobody can take the last 15 years away from us. We lived every moment: Agüero in 2012, the centurions, the treble, Istanbul. Those memories are ours and no verdict changes that. Right now I just feel confused. One thing won’t change, though: whatever happens, I’ll still support the team. This is character-building, as my parents used to say to me. Continue reading...

data.title: Stockpile food – and wash your hands: is that really how to prepare for environmental catastrophe? | George Monbiot
data.description: The UK state is dumping its responsibilities on our doorsteps, while green-lighting policies that lead us closer to crisis Would you mind fixing the NHS? And while you’re at it, could you please build an anti-missile system in your garden? Then regulate the banks, replace the water mains, tax the very rich and use the proceeds to rebuild our schools. Well, come on people: what are you waiting for? I exaggerate, but this isn’t very far from the approach taken by the government’s Prepare campaign . Crucial functions, way beyond the scope of individual action, are dumped on our doorsteps while those in power fail to act. As a result, our national resilience is arguably lower than at any time since the second world war. At the Labour conference last week, Andy Burnham promised “a Britain where people feel the country has got their back again”. To make good on that pledge, he will have to change almost everything. George Monbiot is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: Is Fury v Joshua about meritocratic sporting excellence or just algorithmic celebrity power? | Jonathan Liew
data.description: This long-awaited fight is happening exactly as intended: at the sweet spot where commercial potential meets a genuine absence of jeopardy The 1912 Olympic marathon was held in a brutal Scandinavian heatwave, and before long Shizo Kanakuri of Japan was flagging. His journey to Stockholm had been debilitating; he had barely trained and struggled to sleep. At around the 16-mile mark he finally gave in. Exhausted and disoriented, he stumbled off the road and into a garden party, where – according to his bemused hosts – he sat and drank orange juice for an hour. The next day, deeply ashamed at his failure to complete the race, he quietly took a boat back to Japan. In Sweden the mystery of the “disappearing runner” took on almost mythical proportions. Kanakuri’s name was on the country’s missing persons list for more than 50 years. Continue reading...

data.title: Here’s what connects the Cornell alleged rape case to those before: accused men not being held to serious account | Emma Brockes
data.description: There was progress after #MeToo, but not enough. Certainly not enough to shift the assumptions that still protect men and denigrate victims If the past is another country, and there is nothing so poignant as the innocence of recent history, then there is a third category of engagement with the era directly preceding our own, encapsulated by the line “that didn’t age well”. I found myself thinking about this in relation to news of the seven male students accused of gang-raping a 20-year-old woman two years ago in their fraternity house at Cornell University , and now facing a civil suit brought by their alleged victim. Apparent failures by Cornell and the local district attorney to act appropriately at the time have triggered another round of commentary about the “ death of #MeToo ”, not least with the looming anniversary on 15 October , the date in 2017 when the hashtag first went viral. But the period I find myself thinking about predates even that, when it seemed as if these questions of consent had been largely resolved. Emma Brockes is a Guardian columnist Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: Sam Altman says AI will make ‘bad things’ happen. Exhibit A: needless death | Moustafa Bayoumi
data.description: AI is already implicated in violent deaths and nearly started world war three. Those bad things? data.title: The Guardian view on the US midterms: the cost of living is on the ballot, but this is about democracy too | Editorial
data.description: Donald Trump’s unpopularity and the economic struggles of voters have boosted Democrats. But with less than a month to go, there is no complacency For once, Democrats and Donald Trump might be in agreement: “Pretend I’m on the ticket,” the historically unpopular president has instructed supporters . Midterms are in large part a referendum on the incumbent, and Trump’s war on Iran and its impact on the cost of living have boosted support for Democrats. With less than a month to go, they have reason to be upbeat . The party has a mountain to climb after the devastating defeats of 2024, and the gerrymandering of Republicans, but surveys give it a lead of about nine points on the generic ballot, which measures preference for parties rather than specific candidates. Attention has turned from the prospects of seizing the House, where Democrats are forecast a clear majority, to what once seemed like the highly optimistic possibility of taking the Senate too. That would require flipping four seats , with 35 in play. Remarkably, Democrats are prospering in red states from Texas to Alaska. In Kansas – which Mr Trump carried by 16 points, and which has not elected a Democratic senator since 1932 – the race is neck and neck. Continue reading...

data.title: Havertz, Isak, Dorgu … spate of injuries with national teams leaves sour taste for top clubs
data.description: Premier League clubs, and their European rivals, left with a long list of absentees after a gruelling international break A four-match international break has presented a stress test. “The intensity of the squad, the athleticism of it, really, I think it’s designed for the elite,” said the Wales head coach, Craig Bellamy, on the completion of four matches in 11 days. Elite club coaches would disagree. The Nations League and the wider set of international games staged across the globe have been accompanied by a daily list of casualties, club officials viewing matches through their fingers as players pull up and gesture to the bench. Hamstring and muscle problems have been rife. Sunderland, for example, will be without Brian Brobbey, a key striker, and Dan Ballard, a defensive mainstay, because of strains picked up playing for the Netherlands and Northern Ireland respectively. Bournemouth, yet to win a Premier League match, have lost Alex Scott for up to two months . His performance for England in their 7-0 victory against Croatia won rave reviews, a young player taking his chance and outshining Luka Modric. It came at a heavy cost. A quadriceps injury that had been diagnosed pre-match worsened. “There was zero risk taken from our side,” said Thomas Tuchel. The Bournemouth coach, Marco Rose, is unlikely to see it that way. Continue reading...

That the team have come back to deliver a win in such emphatic fashion was no little achievement. Continue reading...

data.title: Indiana Fever and the Magasphere: a WNBA team’s dangerous path to popularity | Howard Bryant
data.description: Teams have always symbolized division within America. And the Fever have come to prominence during a time of dark political intensity It’s over for now, but no professional sports team spent more time receiving and drawing attention to itself than did the Indiana Fever this season. The Fever has broken, the team eliminated by the defending champion Las Vegas Aces for the second straight season, but Indiana succeeded in being the WNBA’s canary in the coal mine, embodying both the obvious and unintended consequences of rapid growth, while also allowing themselves to be a season-long distraction: part-time professional basketball team, part-time right-wing culture war centerpiece. Less than a decade ago, Atlanta and Minneapolis were praised for their unified political stances. Today, Trumpism has replaced social justice as the defining characteristic of the league – and as the curtain closed on the 2026 WNBA regular season, Indiana stood at its epicenter. The Fever were the most polarizing team in professional sports, known less for their basketball than their culpability in pulling the league from its old cultural identity as a Black/queer league into the current ugliness of the Magasphere – a calculated and dangerous path to popularity. There was the basketball of the WNBA, and then there was the Indiana Fever. This article originally appeared on Howard Bryant’s Substack. You can subscribe here . Continue reading...

data.title: Eckert’s Spygate ban may be lenient, but no sane manager will try the same trick again
data.description: Verdict has been a long time coming and the Southampton head coach has recaptured hearts and minds at St Mary’s “Hi Tonda, are you a cheat?” That simple, succinct, question cut to the heart of a matter that has vexed the Football Association all summer. It was posed by the Northern Echo’s Dominic Shaw after Southampton overcame Middlesbrough in the second leg of May’s Championship playoff semi‑final and proved the cue for Tonda Eckert to walk out of his press conference at St Mary’s. Although Southampton’s manager subsequently admitted to authorising spying on opponents, England’s football authorities struggled to decide what punishment best fitted an act some regard as heinous but which others fail to take seriously. Now, in autumn, we finally have an FA verdict, with Eckert given a six-week ban suspended until the end of the 2027-28 season, a £28,000 fine and a reprimand. Continue reading...

data.title: Comebacks for wild tigers, tuna and sea turtles prove nature loss can be reversed, scientists say
data.description: A landmark report reveals that the world must change the way it produces food to avoid a biodiversity collapse Conservation comebacks for wild tigers, tuna and green​ sea turtles prove that global nature loss can be reversed, ​scientists have said. ​But a report warns food production must be the next ​“positive tipping point​” if the world is to avert biodiversity collapse. The World Wildlife Fund ( WWF ) analysed nearly 36,000 animal populations and more than 5,000 species, producing the largest ever database of vertebrate wildlife. Scientists found populations had declined by an average of 73% since 1970, showing that “nature continues to be degraded at an alarming scale”, with “no sign of losses slowing”. Continue reading...

Polanski, who leads the Greens in England and Wales, is standing for his party in the north London constituency, previously held by Keir Starmer before he stood down as an MP shortly after resigning as prime minister. data.description: Customers are told payment details and passwords were not compromised when employee account was breached Business live – live updates Hackers gained access to names and contact details of millions of customers by impersonating a “trusted contact” to gain access to one of its employee’s accounts, the retailer has said. Thousands of users of the online fashion seller’s app received a notification on Tuesday titled “Asos hacked” with a link to the Telegram messaging service, sending its shares diving by about 10%. data.title: Teenager becomes first person to have testicular tissue transplant in UK
data.description: Operation on 19-year-old who had no sperm after chemotherapy offers hope of preserving children’s fertility after cancer treatment Surgeons have performed the first testicular tissue transplant on a teenager in the UK, offering hope that boys left infertile by chemotherapy could one day have biological children. The 19-year-old had his tissue removed and frozen three years ago before undergoing treatment for a serious blood disorder. He said he was “incredibly grateful” to the medical team behind the pioneering procedure, which represents a potential breakthrough for male fertility preservation. Continue reading...

She was an employee at the anti-plague research institute in the eastern city of Irkutsk, with some reports suggesting she was infected after a workplace accident. Continue reading...

At about 35m hectolitres, the total harvest would be down 2% on a mediocre 2025 yield and 14% below the 2021-2025 average, according to estimates published on Wednesday by the ministry of agriculture. data.title: Cruel torment, depraved violence, evil turns: where did TV’s real baddies go?
data.description: From Carrie’s bullies to Cathy Ames, sympathetic backstories have made villains boring. It’s time to bring back truly awful villains – in all their deliciously sinful glory The new Netflix adaptation of East of Eden largely sticks to the plot of the John Steinbeck novel. There are tweaks – the introduction of a wedding photograph, for example, which becomes a significant item – but otherwise, it is faithful to the book. That is, in terms of the plot. There has already been some discussion about what it has done to Cathy Ames, played with considerable ferocity by Florence Pugh. Cathy, who later changes her name to Kate, kills her parents by burning down the family house. She shoots her husband, Adam, and leaves her baby sons wailing and alone. She slowly poisons the brothel madam Faye, a woman who acts as a mentor to her and treats her as a daughter, while simultaneously tricking her into leaving her everything in her will. In the book, Steinbeck lets Kate reflect on killing Faye. She finds that she has “no feeling” about it at all. She is a brilliant, brutal character, but on television, she becomes something else: complicated. Her cruelty remains intact, but Pugh and showrunner Zoe Kazan have fleshed her out and given reasons for her fury. They invent a scene that implies Cathy was abused as a child by two men in the woods, and when she takes her final bow, the series returns to this moment in flashback, suggesting that her campaign of destruction has been shaped by a life of trauma and pain. In Steinbeck’s hands, Cathy is cold and unfeeling. In the 2020s, Cathy is more sympathetic and less of a brute. Continue reading...

data.title: The Social Reckoning review – Aaron Sorkin’s jittery sequel with all-new evil puppet Zuckerberg
data.description: Jeremy Strong’s slow-talking Facebook founder turns into a cameo, background to a thriller about a whistleblower that somehow never mentions Trump Here is a film for all those people who solemnly deplore social media in conversation but haven’t quite got round to deleting their accounts. Sixteen years have gone by since The Social Network , written by Aaron Sorkin and directed by David Fincher; this was the addictive, obsessive-compulsive movie about the birth of Facebook in Harvard’s macho-competitive cauldron of student sexism and nerdy self-pity, starring Jesse Eisenberg as the fast-talking, arrogant, not-necessarily-evil genius Mark Zuckerberg. Now Sorkin is back with a sequel of sorts, directing his own script – and now Zuckerberg is basically evil, but also weirdly slow talking, as if all the zinging, smart-alecky Sorkinesque dialogue energy of the first film has been siphoned away in early middle age and dispersed among the insurgents in the new cast. Sorkin’s jittery, funny, syncopated style is unmistakable, as distinctive in its way as David Mamet, although he has one joke about “spatula” being a Yiddish word that he has borrowed from Philip Roth’s Portnoy’s Complaint . It is the story of how in 2021, Zuckerberg’s Facebook empire was challenged by courageous whistleblower-employee Frances Haugen and Wall Street Journal investigative reporter Jeff Horwitz, who were on a mission to tell the world how Zuckerberg, scared by falling revenue, changed the algorithm so that engagement was supercharged by rage bait and hate speech, malice and envy. Facebook, moreover, didn’t factcheck political ads, thus driving a huge, nationwide surge in extremist groups and teen bullying and becoming a major player in the Capitol riots. (Having said that, this film does not say aloud the word “Trump” and rather cravenly declines to specify Maga activity.) Continue reading...

data.title: The Uprising review – Paul Greengrass turns revolutionary rage into a Robin Hood origin myth
data.description: Andrew Garfield’s fictional ploughman joins the historical heroes of the 1381 Peasants’ Revolt in a dirt-caked, docudrama-style film with disconcertingly silly moments Paul Greengrass has in fact already made his “uprising” film: United 93 , the gut-wrenching 2006 masterpiece about the passengers onboard United Airlines flight 93 who rose up against the 9/11 hijackers and prevented them from hitting their destination and causing fatalities – except, that is, for those onboard the plane. Greengrass’s new movie, shot in his distinctive handheld, docu-reportage style, is notionally about the 1381 Peasants’ Revolt, in which Wat Tyler and John Ball became legendary for leading an insurrection against the cruel poll tax of Richard II. Or at least … it sort of is. Because the film, in a disconcertingly silly way, imagines the uprising as an origin myth for Robin Hood, or at least someone who’s supposed to be more or less Robin Hood – because that’s not what he’s called and the dates don’t quite match up. Ex-soldier Tyler and radical preacher Ball, capably played by Cosmo Jarvis and Jamie Bell, are joined by a third fictional hero, apparently destined later to canter through the forest with a wealth-redistribution plan. He is a ploughman, known simply as “Ploughman”, played by Andrew Garfield; grieving the loss of his wife and children to the plague and sickened by the tax collectors’ greed and brutality, he instigates an insurrection that soon merges into other outbreaks of revolutionary rage. This involves rivers of smudgy-faced folk in rough clothes descending on the capital from all directions, to demand concessions from the king to whom they are still loyal and believe to have been misled by advisers. Continue reading...

data.title: Gnomes review – Asa Butterfield takes on murderous garden ornaments in pulpy horror-comedy
data.description: Rightly described as ‘Gremlins meets Hot Fuzz’, this fun series has the high-spirit and gusto one hopes for in a show about evil killer gnomes One can never trust marketing materials to accurately describe a movie or TV series, but I’m pleased to report that Gnomes’ official synopsis gets its tone right: “Gremlins meets Hot Fuzz.” This six-part horror-comedy series indeed feels like the kind of rambunctious, high-spirited production that’d be right up the alley of Joe Dante and Edgar Wright, directors of the aforementioned films. Particularly in its air of barely controlled chaos, staged with a slight wink to the audience but never too self-consciously. It’s also – without a doubt – the greatest television series ever made about murderous garden gnomes awakened by an ancient evil. Continue reading...

data.title: Agate Head / Stone Soup by Patricia Lockwood review – a gem of a collection
data.description: Inspired by stones and metals, the memoirist and novelist’s first poetry collection for more than a decade is charming, whimsical and intimate In the introduction to her first book of poetry in 12 years, Patricia Lockwood states that, “For almost a decade … I had not been able to hear it. The poems that I wrote would not end … too much was happening, there was a different kind of attention being paid.” It wasn’t that she didn’t want them to arrive. From Cave Painting: “ And does she still write poems? / Not a whole one since I had been ill. / Five years. I kept saying I was / Doing it privately. So private even / I didn’t know about it.” In that intervening period, Lockwood’s status has jumped from interesting US poet famous for the viral sensation Rape Joke to literary superstar: an acclaimed memoirist and novelist whose freewheeling, antic style is for many the internet’s maelstrom lassoed and put back on to the page. Who else can claim to have turned an audience with the pope into a biting comic essay? Continue reading...

data.title: What the £350 Grand Theft Auto ‘collector’s box’ says about the escalating cost of gaming
data.description: The launch of a collector’s box hints at a new reality: the kinds of games I grew up with are becoming a luxury item, locked behind a forbidding spending barrier • Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here As a parent (and partner) to a habitual collector, I do feel like an unwelcome portion of my life is occupied by an endless war against stuff. Surfaces in my home ceaselessly accumulate piles of random objects: a JoyCon wrist strap, a sticker sheet, an unidentifiable plastic piece of a toy or gizmo, an Xbox 360 controller with no batteries, cases for Switch cartridges lost down the side of the sofa … Stuff encroaches everywhere, especially in a gaming household. Much as I regret the imminent disappearance of physical games , I do not regret the extra space I have in my attic as a result of switching almost entirely to downloaded games over the last decade or so. Speaking of the imminent disappearance of physical games: Rockstar recently announced a £350 ($400) “collector’s box” of Grand Theft Auto 6 goodies … that doesn’t include the game itself. Not even a download code. The Grand Theft Auto VI: The Goodtime State – Vice City Collection, to give it its full and unwieldy name, contains a hat, a bag, a pair of sunglasses, a figurine, a poster and more, including a mirror and a “swizzle spoon” that looks, unambigiously, like a cocaine spoon. The game retails at £70, so if you want something to play alongside all your stuff, you’re looking at an outlay of £420. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘In the wake of death, Courtney Love was giving it her all’: Hole’s Melissa auf der Maur on her best photograph
data.description: ‘This is Courtney doing her makeup on the ’95 Lollapalooza tour. I was documenting my generation being hijacked by corporate greed – and destroyed following the sacrificial death of Kurt Cobain’ When I was going through the archives for my rock photo book, I came across my first ever self-portrait, at Père Lachaise Cemetery in Paris, in front of Jim Morrison’s grave. I am a 13-year-old on an awkward trip with my cool father. He had no respect or interest in Jim Morrison, and that photo is like every photo I’ve taken from that moment on – I’m trying to take agency over what is happening. Photography was the absolute first thing that gave me a feeling of having my own say. It became a way of creating my own universe, one that I could trust. It was absolutely my first love. I was sidetracked into music in a beautiful way by these radical women and a countercultural movement, so the subject of my photographs just changed. It was me within this environment, on stage with Hole, backstage with these luminary, wild people, travelling across the world. My photography followed and morphed with me, and my camera documented my generation being hijacked by corporate greed and destroyed in the wake of the sacrificial death of Kurt Cobain. It was a generational call to document the Lollapalooza ’95 tour, where this photo was taken, for us to understand later. It was also when the wild alternative freaks crossed into the mainstream. Continue reading...

data.title: Only connect: two composers who put humans at the heart of their music, and the conductor who didn’t
data.description: This week, from Reich to Kendall and Celibidache, three musicians who prove there is no such thing as “pure music”, whether we’re talking about a technique, a mode of musical expression or a musician’s legacy. Steve Reich turned 90 on Saturday, and I’ve been thinking about his early tape pieces from the mid-1960s, It’s Gonna Rain and Come Out. They’re such vital works not only because they opened his imagination to what could happen if you made a micro-canon – playing the same material slightly faster or slower – which is what happened when one of his tape machines slipped out of sync with the other: it’s that these are human voices that Reich is setting. It’s Gonna Rain is made from the voice of Brother Walter, a Pentecostal street preacher in San Francisco, whose warning of apocalypse in 1965 Reich recorded and looped against itself, over and over, so that Brother Walter’s voice becomes a wall and wail of sound, a sonic realisation of the sublime inundation he’s announcing. Come Out was made in 1966 with the voice of Daniel Hamm, one of the Harlem Six , six black men wrongly convicted of first-degree murder in New York. Reich’s piece was commissioned for a benefit event for their legal costs as “ background music for passing the hat ”. These pieces don’t just set words, Reich says they “set human beings”, using the vocal recordings not only as musical material but political inspiration and emotional expression. Techniques that are seemingly all about narrowly musical processes – looping, canon-ing, fugue-ing – are embedded in the facts of where they were made and how, and whose voices are being represented by whom. Continue reading...

Techniques that are seemingly all about narrowly musical processes – looping, canon-ing, fugue-ing – are embedded in the facts of where they were made and how, and whose voices are being represented by whom. data.title: ‘Green, red, yellow, blue’? Beneath the surface, diaspora language is anything but Black and white
data.description: Black communities across the globe have large and complex vocabularies to describe race, shaped by their specific cultures and histories Don’t get The Long Wave delivered to your inbox? Sign up here One thing you might not know about this newsletter is how much it is shaped by behind-the-scenes chat. The Long Wave team, and its broader family at the Guardian, is a mini-diaspora in and of itself – one that is constantly in conversation. Often, during our meetings, someone will mention what was assumed to be a quirk of their specific background, only to discover that it is replicated almost entirely across the board. This week, we spoke about the fact that in many of our cultures, there is not just one word for “Black”. “Green”, “red”, “yellow”, “blue”, “wheat”. These are some of the words many tribes in parts of Sudan use to describe complexion. There is no “Black”. I tripped over my words trying to explain to colleagues what these colours denoted – each category is infused with so much cultural depth. In fact, in some cases, they are not even descriptions of complexion, but of features, of broad ethnic background, and even of attractiveness. “Green” means dark, but also implies a sort of uniformity of colour, an even hue, and therefore almost a comeliness. Yellow is lighter, and comes with an unstated connotation of beauty. Blue is the darkest, and is sometimes pejorative, but other times just a description. “Wheat” is the one most likely to be a compliment, a shade that does not diverge too sharply into light or dark. Continue reading...

data.title: Jess Cartner-Morley on fashion: how to wear a leather jacket so it doesn’t wear you
data.description: There’s a lot of Brando badboy baggage attached to this classic outerwear – here’s how to look chic rather than stompy In lots of ways, the arrival of autumn makes getting dressed easier. Not having to shave above your knees. Enough pockets to make a handbag optional. But it’s not all plain sailing. For instance, I don’t think we talk enough about how hard it is to carry off a leather jacket. I thought maybe it was just me. And then I came across Lucinda Chambers – Vogue fashion director for 25 years, now co-curator of gorgeous platform of desirables Collagerie – remarking that she found leather jackets tricky. Lucinda is without a doubt one of the best-dressed women in London, always rocking a strong look – colour, stripes, great jewellery, unexpected shoes – so I was amazed and a bit gratified to find even she struggles. This initiative saw around 500,000 plastic bottles being repurposed, emphasizing sustainability while improving road resilience. As of 2021, trials demonstrated success, reflecting a promising future for eco-friendly road technology. Cumbria is actively expanding this project to broaden its positive environmental impact.

data.title: A shopper paid C$5 for a Bowie painting at an Ontario donation centre; it later sold for C$108,120
data.description: In an astonishing discovery, a seemingly unremarkable painting by David Bowie was acquired for just C$5 at a South River donation center. Once authenticated as DHead XLVI, the artwork soared to a staggering auction price of C$108,120. Experts linked it to Bowie's 1990s oeuvre, showcasing how opportunistic collectors can miss hidden treasures without knowledge of their past.

data.title: South Carolina transfers 2,600 acres of Francis Marion's wartime hideout for conservation
data.description: A 2,600-acre timber property in South Carolina, near the rivers where Revolutionary War commander Francis Marion hid from British forces, has been transferred to the state for conservation. The land forms part of a 7,600-acre project covering more than 60 miles of riverfront, aimed at protecting historic sites, wildlife habitats and floodplains that help reduce flooding.

data.title: East Hampton Land Purchase: town eyes $36.3m Wainscott mine buy; most acres set as open space
data.description: East Hampton Town plans to acquire 38.3 acres of a former sand mine in Wainscott for $36.3 million. The purchase aims to preserve the land for parks and open space, reserving a smaller section for municipal needs. This decision marks a significant change from prior contentious commercial development proposals in the area. A public hearing is set for October 15 to allow residents to voice their opinions.

data.title: Nevada's 700-acre Shakespeare Ranch, listed for $188 million in 2024, now asks $125 million
data.description: Nevada’s historic Shakespeare Ranch, first listed for $188 million in 2024, is now asking $125 million after failing to find a buyer. The 700-acre Lake Tahoe estate features multiple homes, a 465-foot private pier and a barn built in 1873. Despite strong demand for luxury waterfront properties in the region, the ranch remains unsold.

data.title: L’Union africaine lance sa propre agence de notation financière, pour « plus de justice »

data.title: Zeros gerais
data.description: A França tem um importante prêmio literário, o Prix Goncourt, uma espécie de Nobel doméstico, quase tão cobiçado quanto. Existe desde 1903, nunca perdeu um ano e premia um romance específico, não o conjunto de obra. Entre os laureados, Marcel Proust (1919), André Malraux (1933), Elsa Triolet (1944), Simone de Beauvoir (1954), Romain Gary (1956 e 1975), Roger Vailland (1957), Marguerite Duras (1984). Foi criado por Edmond de Goncourt (1822-96), escritor mais conhecido hoje pelo prêmio do que por seus livros. Leia mais (10/08/2026 - 08h00)

data.title: Seca e calor extremos do último El Niño antecipam 'novo normal' nas florestas tropicais
data.description: Cerca de 75% das áreas das florestas tropicais do mundo enfrentaram pelo menos seis meses de seca e calor simultâneos sem precedentes durante o El Niño de 2023-2024. data.title: Mamma förlorade benen i sprängdåd – straff skärps

data.title: Civil buss i Kramatorsk bombad – minst 30 dödade
data.description: Dödstalet stiger efter Rysslands massiva attack på civil infrastruktur och bostäder under onsdagsdygnet. Hittills har minst 30 personer dödats, varav fem barn. data.title: Torbjörn Petersson: EU kommer till Kina för att tala allvar innan det är för sent
data.description: PEKING. Med facit i hand borde EU ha reagerat för tio år sedan. Men då fanns ingen insikt om hur snabbt Kina skulle utvecklas. I dag strömmar kinesiska varor in i Europa som riskerar att krossa avgörande delar av EU:s industri. Ett möte i Peking måste ge en vink om att det finns en väg framåt – annars ökar risken för handelskrig.

data.title: Expert: Ömsesidig hotbild mellan veterinärer och djurägare

data.title: Útoky inspirují další. Bývalý žák ve škole u Varšavy zabil jednoho člověka, dva zranil
data.description: Na základní škole nedaleko Wyszkowa severovýchodně od Varšavy bývalý žák napadl ostrým předmětem tři lidi – jeden z nich zemřel a dva jsou zranění, oznámila policie. Policejní mluvčí Ilona Puścianová řekla, že napadenými jsou školnice, jedna z učitelek a ředitel. Policie v Mazovském vojvodství, kde se útok stal, později oznámila, že i přes snahy o oživení zemřela 37letá zaměstnankyně školy. Podle serveru onet.pl šlo o školnici.

data.title: „Neodpovídá to skutečnosti.“ Rusko popírá nákazu morem u dalšího člověka
data.description: Ruské úřady popřely zprávy, že se v sibiřském ústavu pro boj proti moru nakazil další zaměstnanec. Laborantka zmíněného irkutského ústavu podle ruských médií nedávno zemřela na plicní mor, zatímco ruské úřady výskyt moru popírají a tvrdí, že mladá žena podlehla zápalu plic nezjištěného původu. O informace o nákaze požádala ruské úřady Světová zdravotnická organizace (WHO).

data.description: Svářeč Libor Jurčík obžalovaný z loňského neúmyslného zapálení střechy školy na sídlišti Jižní Svahy ve Zlíně ve čtvrtek u zlínského okresního soudu připustil, že při její opravě porušil předpisy. data.title: Rakušan je pro elektronizaci voleb. Umožnila by to, po čem volá Pavlová
data.description: Šéf hnutí STAN, bývalý ministr vnitra Vít Rakušan, je pro postupnou elektronizaci voleb, která by umožnila na dálku volit občanům i v komunálních volbách. Kdyby to bylo možné, nemuselo by se ani řešit, že dal prezident Petr Pavel přednost soukromé zahraniční dovolené v Maroku před komunálními volbami, které se konají v pátek a v sobotu spolu s prvním koleb voleb senátních.

data.title: Rusové zasáhli klouzavými bombami linkové autobusy, zabili třicet lidí
data.description: Třicet lidí přišlo o život při ruském útoku na Kramatorsk ve východoukrajinské Doněcké oblasti, informoval šéf regionální civilní a vojenské správy Vadym Filaškin. Dalších 18 lidí je zraněných. Prokuratura už dříve uvedla, že Rusové pravděpodobně použili klouzavé letecké bomby, které zasáhly dva linkové autobusy. Útok vyšetřuje kvůli podezření ze spáchání válečného zločinu.

data.title: Kurzy zamíchal Michal David, v Praze je to těsné. Bookmakeři o favoritech voleb
data.description: Kdo bude příští pražský primátor? Dotlačí koncerty Michala Davida Sandru Tsoukernik nebo „nejhorší volební song“ Ty hejtmane Jana Grolicha do Senátu? A kolik hlasů dostane bývalý pornoherec Robert Rosenberg? V sázkových kancelářích se v těchto dnech nesází jen na to, kolik gólů dostanou čeští fotbalisté od Španělů nebo Angličanů, ale také na úspěch stran a kandidátů v senátních a komunálních volbách.

data.title: Naštvaní francouzští studenti mají hymnu. Do ulic i na sítě vyrážejí s písní z dětství
data.description: Neoficiální hymnou francouzských studentů protestujících proti nedostatku financí a personálu ve školství i stavu budov se stal jedenáct let starý soundtrack krátkého filmu na YouTube. Demonstrací, které v posledních dnech otřásají Francií, se účastní stovky tisíc středoškoláků generace Z, pro které je píseň z dětství nyní protestsongem.

data.title: Zemřel herec Miloslav Kopečný, vekslák Slepejš z filmu Bony a klid. Bylo mu 82 let
data.description: Ve věku 82 zemřel herec Miloslav Kopečný, rodák z Třebíče. Jeho nejznámější postava byl šmelinář s přezdívkou Slepejš z filmu Bony a klid režiséra Víta Olmera. Hrál i ve volném pokračování Bony a klid 2. Dále hrál ve filmech Kalamita, Rozpuštěný a vypuštěný, Kousek nebe nebo Vlny. Zpráva o jeho odchodu se objevila na facebooku Divadla Palace.

data.title: Meteorologové varují před silným větrem. Ve dvou oblastech zesílí na 70 km v hodině
data.description: V Krušných horách a na Českomoravské vrchovině a v okolí bude od dnešního odpoledne foukat silný vítr, který v nárazech může dosáhnout rychlosti až 70 kilometrů v hodině. V noci pak částečně zeslábne, informoval Český hydrometeorologický ústav. Podle něj se vítr objeví v Česku při přechodu studené fronty, ve zmíněných oblastech by ale měl být nejsilnější.

data.title: I ve volbách v Česku rozhoduje los. Kdy na něj skutečně dojde?
data.description: Výsledky komunálních voleb nejsou vždy pouze o vůli občanů. O tom, kdo nakonec skutečně získá mandáty v obecních zastupitelstvech, může rozhodnout i losování. Dochází k němu ale jen výjimečně, pokud voliči stranám odevzdají stejný počet hlasů. Tahání „kratší sirky“ však neřeší všechny sporné výsledky – u senátních voleb je to jinak.

data.title: Místo obratiště má být blíž zástavbě tramvajová smyčka. Místní se obávají hluku a otřesů
data.description: Značný rozruch vyvolala na Severním Předměstí Plzně změna projektu na vybudování tramvajové trati, která má sloužit především obyvatelům sídlišť Vinice a Sylván. Dotčení lidé v posledních dnech zjistili, že místo dříve plánovaného úvraťového obratiště, kde by se oboustranné tramvaje vracely na cestu k centru města, má o kus dál vzniknout klasická tramvajová smyčka. Ta zabere víc místa a přiblíží se k bytovým domům.

data.title: Mladík při zadržení nekladl odpor, přesto ho policista zbil. Teď čelí obžalobě
data.description: Video v květnu obletělo sociální sítě. Mladík v Českých Budějovicích utíká před policejní hlídkou, ale následně se otáčí a s rukama nad hlavou se vzdává. data.title: Demokracie se umí bránit: jak Řecko zlikvidovalo Zlatý úsvit a co z toho plyne pro AfD
data.description: Uteklo šest let od chvíle, kdy padly dlouholeté tresty pro nejvyšší představitele neonacistické strany Zlatý úsvit. Řecká justice tím fakticky uzavřela jednu z nejvýznamnějších kapitol svých moderních právních dějin. Tento proces se stal klíčovým precedentem pro celou současnou Evropu, která se potýká s novou vlnou radikalismu. Ukázal totiž, že demokratický právní stát může mít k dispozici efektivní a legální nástroje, jak eliminovat síly, které ho chtějí rozložit zevnitř.

data.title: Letadlovka Abraham Lincoln s psychicky zdeptanou posádkou připlouvá domů
data.description: Americká letadlová loď USS Abraham Lincoln se vrací do svého domovského přístavu v San Diegu, kde by měla zakotvit ve čtvrtek. Loď byla nasazena na moři od loňského listopadu. Námořníky ve středu navštívil americký ministr obrany Pete Hegseth, který chválil jejich odolnost. Podle médií se však dlouhá doba nasazení projevila na duševním stavu personálu.

data.title: Hormuz transits at lowest in over two months after attacks, data shows
data.description: Transits through the Strait of Hormuz have dropped to the lowest level in over two months, with only seven vessels passing through recently amid increased attacks on tankers, according to shipping data. Crude oil crossings fell by 27 percent from the previous week, now at 10.1 million barrels per day, while exports from the Gulf of Oman and the Red Sea rose significantly, compensating for the reduced supply through Hormuz.

data.title: A Boda, la hausse des prix de produits de premières nécessité affecte les ménages
data.description: Fr : Sa : Une partie des habitants de Boda (Lobaye) dénonce la hausse des prix de plusieurs denrées alimentaires. Selon eux, certains produits se font de plus en plus rares sur les marchés de la ville. Cette rareté pèse à la fois sur les ménages et les commerçants. Correspondance de Laure Fortuna Mbossé. L’article A Boda, la hausse des prix de produits de premières nécessité affecte les ménages est apparu en premier sur Radio Ndeke Luka .

data.title: Retour au calme à Ilebo après 4 jours d'affrontements meurtriers
data.description: La quiétude est revenue, mercredi 7 octobre, dans le territoire d'Ilebo (Kasaï) après quatre jours d'affrontements violents, soit du 3 au 6 octobre, entre deux groupes de jeunes. Trois personnes ont été tuées et plusieurs autres blessées à la suite de ces heurts provoqués par un litige foncier familial. L’intervention des forces de l'ordre et l'interpellation de 18 jeunes impliqués a permis de restaurer le calme dans la cité d’Ilebo.

data.title: Beni : hausse du prix du carburant sur fond de litige fiscal entre la FEC et l’ACCAD à Kasindi
data.description: La ville de Beni, dans le Nord-Kivu, fait face à une brusque augmentation du prix du carburant en raison du blocage de plus de 300 camions-citernes au poste frontalier de Kasindi. La Fédération des entreprises du Congo (FEC) accuse l’Association congolaise des commissionnaires agréés en douane (ACCAD) d'exiger une surtaxe litigieuse avant de libérer les cargaisons, ce qui perturbe l'approvisionnement local et pèse sur le pouvoir d'achat des ménages.

data.title: Askofu Zacharie Katanda Masimango wa Dayosisi ya Anglikana ya Kindu: Viongozi wa dini wazungumzia Imani wakati wa Ebola.
data.description: Viongozi wa dini jimboni Maniema pia wanajipanga kupambana na Ebola. Mjini Kindu, dayosisi ya Anglikana inafanya juhudi kubwa kuelimisha wakaaji kuhusu ugonjwa huo. Kikao kwa ajili ya viongozi wa dini kiliandaliwa na mada kuu ilikua  "Imani wakati wa Ebola," kwa lengo la kuwapa viongozi wale mitazamo sahihi na ujumbe bora wa kuwafikishia waumini wao. Ili kujadili suala hili, Florence Kiza Lunga anazungumza na Askofu Zacharie Katanda Masimango wa Dayosisi ya Anglikana ya Kindu.

data.description: Le ministre des Droits humains, Samuel Mbemba, plaide pour que le Barreau de Kinshasa-Gombe ouvre ses portes aux diplômés en droit issus des universités privées agréées ou reconnues en République démocratique du Congo. data.title: Plus d’un million d'euros investis pour la modernisation de l'Hôpital général de référence de Komanda (Ituri)
data.description: L’Hôpital général de référence de Komanda, en Ituri, est doté de nouvelles infrastructures modernes financées par l’Union européenne, via l’Université libre de Bruxelles (ULB-Coopération), pour un montant global de plus d’un million trois cent mille euros. Ces infrastructures ont été inaugurées, mardi 6 octobre 2026. Le projet comprend quatre nouveaux pavillons, deux forages d'eau potable ainsi qu'un système d'autonomie énergétique solaire.

data.title: Multiplicité de cas d'escroqueries à Kinshasa : un cabinet d’avocats lance un SOS
data.description: Face au regain de cas d’escroquerie à Kinshasa, KTF Lawyers, un cabinet d’avocats basé dans la capitale congolaise, appelle la population locale à la vigilance. Frédéric Kwamba Tshingej, avocat au barreau de Kinshasa-Gombe, affirme que son cabinet a enregistré une dizaine de cas en une semaine. Il cite notamment des escroqueries immobilières.

data.title: Les FARDC annoncent la reddition de 17 combattants de la coalition AFC-M23/Twiraneho à Fizi
data.description: Les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) ont annoncé, mercredi 7 octobre, la reddition de dix-sept combattants de la coalition AFC-M23/Twiraneho mardi 6 octobre dans les Hauts Plateaux du territoire de Fizi, au Sud-Kivu. Selon l’armée, les redditions ont eu lieu à Abala, Nyaruhinga et Kabanja. Un autre combattant a été capturé lors des combats dans cette région.

data.title: Ebola à Beni : 8 malades guéris quittent le Centre de traitement
data.description: Huit patients guéris de la maladie à virus Ebola ont quitté, ce mercredi 7 octobre, le Centre de traitement d’Ebola de Beni. Parmi eux, figure un nourrisson âgé d’un mois. Ces nouvelles guérisons interviennent quatre jours seulement après la sortie de dix autres patients déclarés guéris, renforçant l’espoir au sein des communautés touchées par l’épidémie.

data.title: Coachs sur les réseaux sociaux :  Un phénomène à la mode
data.description: Sur TikTok, Facebook et d’autres plateformes, ils sont de plus en plus nombreux à se présenter comme des « coachs » et à partager des conseils sur l’amour, les relations familiales, le bien-être, le business, la mode, la beauté ou encore le développement personnel. À travers leurs vidéos, certains rassemblent des communautés de plusieurs centaines de milliers, voire de millions d’abonnés. Mais derrière cette popularité, une question se pose : quelles sont leurs compétences et quelle valeur accorder à leurs conseils ?

data.title: MAA, KSrelief sign joint implementation programme for 20 solar-powered boreholes in Ghana
data.description:
MAA and KSrelief sign Joint Implementation Programme for 20 solar-powered boreholes in Ghana

Markaz Aleawn Alyaqin Humanitarian Services (MAA) and the King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre (KSrelief) have signed a Joint Implementation Programme (JIP) for the construction of 20 solar-powered boreholes across five regions of Ghana.

The JIP was signed at the KSrelief headquarters in Riyadh and will be implemented over a period of eight months, benefiting an estimated 76,555 people in schools and communities.

The beneficiary locations include Asawase M/A Cluster of Schools, Sepe Cluster of Schools, Akrom Cluster of Schools, Garden City Special School, Sakafia Islamic Senior High School, Parkoso Senior High School, Kumasi Academy, New Konkrompe Senior High School and the University of Energy and Natural Resources (UENR).

Other beneficiary communities include Techimantia, Vea, Bongo Gurigo, Kudorogo, Kofiase, Bepoase, Sawua, Kokoado, Homabenase, Badaase and Aboabo No. 1–4, among others.

Under the programme, each facility will comprise a solar-powered borehole, a 10-cubic-metre water storage tank and six water taps, providing sustainable access to safe water for drinking, sanitation, hygiene and other essential needs.

The project forms part of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia’s continuing humanitarian and relief efforts through KSrelief, which extend to communities in need around the world and seek to provide sustainable solutions that contribute to improving living conditions.

Markaz Aleawn Alyaqin Humanitarian Services has expressed its sincere gratitude to the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and His Royal Highness Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince and Prime Minister, for their continued support for humanitarian and relief efforts worldwide.

MAA also extended its appreciation to Dr Abdullah A. Al-Rabeeah, Advisor at the Royal Court and Supervisor General of KSrelief, and Eng. Ahmed bin Ali Al-Baiz, Assistant Supervisor General for Operations and Programs, for their continued commitment to humanitarian service and cooperation.

data.title: ECG warns customers against fake meter sales, MoMo fraud
data.description:
The Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) has warned customers across the country against fraudsters posing as its staff or agents to sell fake meters and demand payments through personal mobile money accounts.

The company says customers should not send money to private MoMo numbers for electricity services.

ECG General Manager for External Communications, Dr Charles Nii Ayiku Ayiku, said the company operates a fully cashless payment system, with customers required to make payments through official channels.

“ECG runs a fully cashless system,” Dr Ayiku said. “All payments must go through the ECG Power App or the shortcode *226#. Money sent to a personal MoMo number does not reach the company and will not reflect on your account.”

Dr Ayiku identified the sale of meters by individuals as one of the schemes being used to defraud customers.

He said some individuals pose as ECG staff or agents and offer to supply and install new meters for a fee.

data.title: 18 groupes électrogènes russes pour renforcer la production de la JIRAMA
data.description: Le gouvernement accélère ses initiatives pour faire face à la crise énergétique. La JIRAMA a reçu l'ordre de procéder à l'acquisition de 18 groupes électrogènes auprès de Malmekhservice, une entreprise de droit russe. Cette opération, décidée dans le cadre de l'état d'urgence énergétique, sera réalisée sans appel d'offres. Chaque équipement devrait développer une puissance de 1 mégawatt, selon les indications d'un technicien de la compagnie nationale. Les installations permettraient ainsi (…) - Energie

data.title: Education nationale : les agents maintiennent la pression pour trois mois de rappel
data.description: La mobilisation se poursuit au ministère de l'Éducation nationale. Ce mercredi, les personnels administratifs et techniques syndiqués maintiennent leur mouvement pour obtenir l'application rétroactive de leur indemnité de technicité. D'un montant de 150 000 ariary, celle-ci constitue aujourd'hui le principal point de désaccord entre les agents et l'administration. Les grévistes ne contestent plus seulement le principe du versement de cette indemnité. C'est désormais son calendrier (…) - Société

data.description: Madagascar progresse légèrement en matière de transparence budgétaire, mais reste encore loin du niveau jugé satisfaisant. Les résultats de l'Enquête sur le budget ouvert (EBO) 2025, réalisée par MSIS Tatao, et présentée mardi 6 octobre, font apparaître des insuffisances importantes, aussi bien dans l'accès aux informations que dans la participation citoyenne et le contrôle des finances publiques. La transparence budgétaire obtient une note de 44/100, contre 39/100 lors de la précédente (…) - Economie

data.description: L'intervention policière meurtrière survenue le 1er octobre à Namontana prend désormais une tournure judiciaire et polémique. La famille de l'employé décédé ainsi que le gérant de La Gastro Pizza ont déposé plainte au Toby Ratsimandrava. data.title: Gouvernement : Mamitiana Rajaonarison dresse un bilan positif de son premier semestre
data.description: Six mois après sa nomination à la tête du gouvernement, Mamitiana Rajaonarison a présenté le bilan de l'action de son équipe lors d'une intervention sur la TVM. data.description: L'actualité de la fin de semaine a été marquée par une nouvelle bavure policière du côté de Namontana. Des éléments d'une unité d'intervention de la Police nationale ont tiré sur un groupe d'employés de Gastro Pizza Soanierana qui rentrait après leur service. L'information qui se propage d'abord rapidement sur les réseaux sociaux est que ces policiers étaient ivres. Contre-attaque de leur institution pour justifier les tirs intempestifs qui auraient tué une personne et en auraient blessé (…) - Editorial

data.title: Ever Bonilla, el comerciante asesinado a balazos en barrio Lempira de San Pedro Sula
data.description: Como Ever Gamaliel Bonilla Muñoz, de 40 años, fue identificado el hombre que murió tras recibir varios impactos de bala este miércoles en el barrio Lempira de San Pedro Sula. De acuerdo con información proporcionada por una prima de la víctima, Ever Bonilla Muñoz se encontraba en el sector realizando mandados en compañía de una familiar cuando habría sido atacado por sujetos que presuntamente intentaban asaltarlo. Según información preliminar proporcionada por las autoridades, varios sujetos armados habrían interceptado al hombre y le dispararon en reiteradas ocasiones durante el supuesto asalto. El ataque ocurrió en la 7 calle, entre la 7 y 8 avenidas del barrio Lempira, donde el cuerpo de Bonilla Muñoz quedó tendido sobre el pavimento. La mujer que acompañaba a la víctima resultó ilesa, pero quedó conmocionada tras presenciar el ataque, según personas que se encontraban en el lugar. Al momento del hecho, Bonilla Muñoz vestía una camisa roja, jeans azules y tenis negros. Ever era un reconocido comerciante, tenía un mercadito en la 27 calle de San Pedro Sula, según cercanos a la víctima. Tras recibir una llamada de emergencia, agentes de la Policía Nacional se desplazaron hasta el lugar y acordonaron la escena para proteger posibles indicios que contribuyan a esclarecer el crimen. Personal de Medicina Forense realizó el levantamiento del cuerpo y el procedimiento correspondiente. Las autoridades investigan las circunstancias en las que ocurrió el ataque y buscan establecer quiénes serían los responsables de la muerte de Bonilla Muñoz. El posible asalto permanece como una de las líneas de investigación y deberá ser confirmado o descartado conforme avancen las diligencias. La víctima había sido identificada preliminarmente como Ever Muñoz, de entre 40 y 45 años. Posteriormente, familiares confirmaron su identidad como Ever Gamaliel Bonilla Muñoz, de 40 años. La investigación continúa para determinar el móvil del crimen y esclarecer la participación de los sujetos que habrían cometido el ataque.

data.title: Matan a balazos a un hombre en el barrio Lempira de San Pedro Sula
data.description: San Pedro Sula, Cortés. De varios impactos de bala fue asesinado un hombre este miércoles en el barrio Lempira de San Pedro Sula, en un hecho que es investigado por las autoridades. La víctima fue preliminarmente identificada como Ever Muñoz , de entre 40 y 45 años, cuyo cuerpo quedó tendido en el suelo en la 7 calle , entre la 7 y 8 avenidas del referido sector. Según información preliminar proporcionada por las autoridades, sujetos armados habrían interceptado al hombre con la intención de asaltarlo y le dispararon en reiteradas ocasiones. Las autoridades manejan de manera preliminar el asalto como posible móvil del crimen, aunque esta hipótesis deberá ser confirmada o descartada conforme avancen las investigaciones. De acuerdo con testigos, Muñoz se encontraba en San Pedro Sula realizando mandados en compañía de una familiar cuando ocurrió el ataque. La mujer que lo acompañaba resultó ilesa, pero quedó conmocionada tras presenciar la muerte de su familiar, según personas que se encontraban en el lugar. El cuerpo de Muñoz quedó sobre el pavimento y, al momento del hecho, vestía una camisa roja, jeans azules y tenis negros. Tras recibir una llamada de emergencia, agentes de la Policía Nacional se desplazaron hasta el lugar y acordonaron la escena para evitar la alteración de posibles indicios relacionados con el crimen. Personal de Medicina Forense se encontraba a la espera para realizar el levantamiento del cuerpo y determinar mediante los procedimientos correspondientes la identidad de la víctima y otros elementos de interés para la investigación. Mientras avanzan las diligencias, las autoridades buscan establecer cómo ocurrió el ataque y quiénes serían los responsables de la muerte de Ever Muñoz. El posible asalto permanece como una de las líneas de investigación.

data.title: Más de 3,200 policías refuerzan seguridad durante el Feriado Morazánico en SPS
data.description: San Pedro Sula, Cortés. Más de 3,200 funcionarios policiales fueron destinados a labores preventivas durante el Feriado Morazánico , como parte del plan de seguridad implementado para proteger a los viajeros y reducir la incidencia delictiva durante el asueto. Alejandro Valladares , portavoz de la Policía Nacional, explicó que los operativos se mantienen antes, durante y después del feriado, con especial atención en lugares donde se concentra una mayor cantidad de personas, como la Gran Central Metropolitana de San Pedro Sula . En la terminal sampedrana, los agentes realizan operativos focalizados que incluyen la verificación de documentación de pasajeros y acciones para detectar personas con órdenes de captura pendientes, además de prevenir la portación ilegal de armas, robos y asaltos. “Algunas de las actividades operativas es revisar a las personas su documentación, se les solicita para identificar si hay personas que tienen órdenes judiciales o de aprehensión pendientes, evitar de hecho que anden portando armas de forma ilegal, así mismo todo tipo de robos y asaltos y que de igual manera haya una mayor respuesta en algún tipo de emergencias”, explicó Valladares. El portavoz señaló que el despliegue también se extiende a los principales ejes carreteros y destinos turísticos de la zona norte del país, en coordinación con las instituciones que integran la Comisión Nacional de Prevención en Movilizaciones Masivas (Conaprem). Valladares informó que los operativos de seguridad también se mantienen en el transporte público, mediante abordajes y desabordajes en diferentes rutas que conectan San Pedro Sula con Choloma, el norte del departamento y otros sectores. El objetivo, explicó, es mantener presencia policial en puntos de alta circulación y prevenir hechos delictivos durante los días de mayor movilización. La Policía también mantiene presencia en lugares turísticos, como playas y balnearios , debido a que durante estas fechas aumenta la cantidad de personas que se desplazan hacia esos sitios. Además del despliegue policial, Valladares recomendó a los ciudadanos adoptar medidas de prevención durante sus viajes, entre ellas evitar publicar en redes sociales información sobre sus planes, destinos o ubicaciones. El portavoz también hizo un llamado a los conductores para que revisen las condiciones de sus vehículos antes de emprender un viaje y eviten ingerir bebidas alcohólicas si van a conducir. Valladares recordó que durante estos periodos se realizan revisiones físico-mecánicas de vehículos en coordinación con el Instituto Hondureño de Transporte Terrestre (IHTT) y otras instituciones. Asimismo, pidió a los conductores evitar el consumo de bebidas alcohólicas antes de manejar, debido al riesgo que representa para ellos y para otras personas. “Es importante no ingerir bebidas alcohólicas si va a conducir debido a que pone su vida en riesgo y la de terceros”, enfatizó. La Policía Nacional mantiene el llamado a los ciudadanos para que adopten medidas de prevención y reporten cualquier emergencia durante el Feriado Morazánico.

data.title: Viajeros abarrotan la Gran Central Metropolitana de SPS por el Feriado Morazánico
data.description: San Pedro Sula, Cortés. Desde las primeras horas de este miércoles, la Gran Central Metropolitana de San Pedro Sula registra una alta afluencia de pasajeros que aprovechan el Feriado Morazánico para trasladarse hacia sus lugares de origen, visitar a familiares o conocer diferentes destinos del país. El movimiento de viajeros comenzó a ser evidente en las diferentes áreas de la terminal , donde decenas de personas esperaban abordar los buses que los llevarían hacia distintas ciudades. Entre los destinos con mayor demanda se encuentran Comayagua y Siguatepeque, además de otros puntos del occidente del país, como Santa Rosa de Copán y Copán Ruinas. También se reporta movimiento de pasajeros con destino hacia Olanchito. Algunos viajeros consultados señalaron que aprovecharán el feriado para visitar a sus familiares y realizar turismo dentro de Honduras. Una pasajera que se dirigía hacia Siguatepeque explicó que viajaría para visitar a sus familiares y que prefería permanecer en el país durante el asueto. Otro viajero, con destino a Comayagua, manifestó que su intención era visitar a su familia y continuar conociendo la cultura y los diferentes lugares de Honduras. Aunque la terminal registra movimiento de pasajeros, algunos viajeros consultados consideraron que la afluencia era similar a la de otros años y la calificaron como normal para este periodo. Las empresas de transporte que operan desde la Gran Central Metropolitana mantendrán sus horarios habituales durante el Feriado Morazánico , de acuerdo con lo informado previamente por representantes del sector. Los usuarios que tienen previsto viajar durante el asueto podrán abordar las unidades que cubren las diferentes rutas desde la terminal sampedrana. El Feriado Morazánico representa uno de los principales periodos de movilización interna en Honduras, con miles de personas que aprovechan los días de descanso para visitar a familiares o desplazarse hacia destinos turísticos.
